lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: name: setup-matt-pocock-skills

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: description: Configure this repo for the engineering skills — set up its issue tracker, triage label vocabulary, and domain doc layout. Run once before first use of the other engineering skills.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: disable-model-invocation: true

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: # Setup Matt Pocock's Skills

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Scaffold the per-repo configuration that the engineering skills assume:

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Issue tracker** — where issues live (GitHub by default; local markdown is also supported out of the box)

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Triage labels** — the strings used for the five canonical triage roles

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Domain docs** — where `CONTEXT.md` and ADRs live, and the consumer rules for reading them

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: This is a prompt-driven skill, not a deterministic script. Explore, present what you found, confirm with the user, then write.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Process

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ### 1. Explore

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Look at the current repo to understand its starting state. Read whatever exists; don't assume:

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - `git remote -v` and `.git/config` — is this a GitHub repo? Which one?

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` at the repo root — does either exist? Is there already an `## Agent skills` section in either?

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - `CONTEXT.md` and `CONTEXT-MAP.md` at the repo root

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - `docs/adr/` and any `src/*/docs/adr/` directories

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - `docs/agents/` — does this skill's prior output already exist?

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - `.scratch/` — sign that a local-markdown issue tracker convention is already in use

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ### 2. Present findings and ask

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Summarise what's present and what's missing. Then walk the user through the three decisions **one at a time** — present a section, get the user's answer, then move to the next. Don't dump all three at once.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Assume the user does not know what these terms mean. Each section starts with a short explainer (what it is, why these skills need it, what changes if they pick differently). Then show the choices and the default.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: **Section A — Issue tracker.**

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: > Explainer: The "issue tracker" is where issues live for this repo. Skills like `to-issues`, `triage`, `to-prd`, and `qa` read from and write to it — they need to know whether to call `gh issue create`, write a markdown file under `.scratch/`, or follow some other workflow you describe. Pick the place you actually track work for this repo.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Default posture: these skills were designed for GitHub. If a `git remote` points at GitHub, propose that. If a `git remote` points at GitLab (`gitlab.com` or a self-hosted host), propose GitLab. Otherwise (or if the user prefers), offer:

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **GitHub** — issues live in the repo's GitHub Issues (uses the `gh` CLI)

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **GitLab** — issues live in the repo's GitLab Issues (uses the [`glab`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli) CLI)

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Local markdown** — issues live as files under `.scratch/<feature>/` in this repo (good for solo projects or repos without a remote)

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Other** (Jira, Linear, etc.) — ask the user to describe the workflow in one paragraph; the skill will record it as freeform prose

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: If — and only if — the user picked **GitHub** or **GitLab**, ask one follow-up:

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: > Explainer: Open-source repos often receive feature requests as pull requests, not just issues — a PR is an issue with attached code. If you turn this on, `/triage` pulls *external* PRs into the same queue and runs them through the same labels and states as issues (collaborators' in-flight PRs are left alone). Leave it off if PRs aren't a request surface for you.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **PRs as a request surface** — yes / no (default: no). Record the answer in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`. For local-markdown and other trackers, skip this question — there are no PRs.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: **Section B — Triage label vocabulary.**

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: > Explainer: When the `triage` skill processes an incoming issue, it moves it through a state machine — needs evaluation, waiting on reporter, ready for an AFK agent to pick up, ready for a human, or won't fix. To do that, it needs to apply labels (or the equivalent in your issue tracker) that match strings *you've actually configured*. If your repo already uses different label names (e.g. `bug:triage` instead of `needs-triage`), map them here so the skill applies the right ones instead of creating duplicates.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: The five canonical roles:

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - `needs-triage` — maintainer needs to evaluate

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - `needs-info` — waiting on reporter

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - `ready-for-agent` — fully specified, AFK-ready (an agent can pick it up with no human context)

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - `ready-for-human` — needs human implementation

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - `wontfix` — will not be actioned

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Default: each role's string equals its name. Ask the user if they want to override any. If their issue tracker has no existing labels, the defaults are fine.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: **Section C — Domain docs.**

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: > Explainer: Some skills (`improve-codebase-architecture`, `diagnosing-bugs`, `tdd`) read a `CONTEXT.md` file to learn the project's domain language, and `docs/adr/` for past architectural decisions. They need to know whether the repo has one global context or multiple (e.g. a monorepo with separate frontend/backend contexts) so they look in the right place.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Confirm the layout:

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Single-context** — one `CONTEXT.md` + `docs/adr/` at the repo root. Most repos are this.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Multi-context** — `CONTEXT-MAP.md` at the root pointing to per-context `CONTEXT.md` files (typically a monorepo).

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ### 3. Confirm and edit

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Show the user a draft of:

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - The `## Agent skills` block to add to whichever of `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` is being edited (see step 4 for selection rules)

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - The contents of `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`, `docs/agents/triage-labels.md`, `docs/agents/domain.md`

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Let them edit before writing.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ### 4. Write

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: **Pick the file to edit:**

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - If `CLAUDE.md` exists, edit it.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - Else if `AGENTS.md` exists, edit it.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - If neither exists, ask the user which one to create — don't pick for them.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Never create `AGENTS.md` when `CLAUDE.md` already exists (or vice versa) — always edit the one that's already there.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: If an `## Agent skills` block already exists in the chosen file, update its contents in-place rather than appending a duplicate. Don't overwrite user edits to the surrounding sections.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: The block:

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ```markdown

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Agent skills

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ### Issue tracker

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: [one-line summary of where issues are tracked, plus whether external PRs are a triage surface]. See `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ### Triage labels

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: [one-line summary of the label vocabulary]. See `docs/agents/triage-labels.md`.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ### Domain docs

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: [one-line summary of layout — "single-context" or "multi-context"]. See `docs/agents/domain.md`.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Then write the three docs files using the seed templates in this skill folder as a starting point:

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - [issue-tracker-github.md](./issue-tracker-github.md) — GitHub issue tracker

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - [issue-tracker-gitlab.md](./issue-tracker-gitlab.md) — GitLab issue tracker

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - [issue-tracker-local.md](./issue-tracker-local.md) — local-markdown issue tracker

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - [triage-labels.md](./triage-labels.md) — label mapping

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - [domain.md](./domain.md) — domain doc consumer rules + layout

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: For "other" issue trackers, write `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` from scratch using the user's description.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ### 5. Done

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Tell the user the setup is complete and which engineering skills will now read from these files. Mention they can edit `docs/agents/*.md` directly later — re-running this skill is only necessary if they want to switch issue trackers or restart from scratch.
